deterministic.summary: HV loss was the BMS under-voltage protection acting (protective response, not the origin). Open upstream explanations: SOC estimation / calibration error; Usable capacity far below the stated parameter; Current under-measured or load bypassing the sensor. The recorded data does not separate them. A weak cell cannot explain the whole incident on its own: the highest cell was also depleted (pack-wide decline larger than the cell spread), and the SOC accounting discrepancy is pack-level: a weak cell can be an additional contributor, not the whole explanation. No root cause is confirmed.

result.headline: Under-voltage trip after SOC jumped 38 points unexplained by counted charge; upstream cause not separable from this data.
result.explanation: BMS opened the contactors on cell under-voltage (protective response). SOC tracked counted charge, then was re-stated 60.8 to 22.8 % without charge. SOC calibration error, low usable capacity or under-read current all fit.

evidence.quote: CHANGE battery.soc[bms] at t=1597 s: 43.2 -> 27.2 % (step -16, 10x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: Abrupt SOC re-statement. The physical check puts the full 60.8 to 22.8 % correction at 1576.5-1606.5 s, with 0.0545 Ah measured and 37.95 pp unexplained.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT battery.pack_current held 6.54 from t=0 to 2100 s (4201 samples)
evidence.shows: Steady 6.54 A discharge. SOC tracked this counted charge between corrections (ratios 1.101 and 0.892), so the estimator was counting charge.
Fault level 3 at 2100.5 s, with both main contactors opening at the same instant (lines 19-20). This is the protective response, not the origin.

evidence.quote: SHIFT battery.cell_voltage[min] changed level for good at t=640 s: median 3.2 before, 2.864 after V (2240x its variation before)
evidence.shows: The whole pack declined: the highest cell fell 450 mV against a 260 mV spread at the trip. A single weak cell cannot explain this.
Escalation 1 at 1453 s, 2 at 1799 s, 3 at 2100.5 s. Warnings began well before the trip while SOC still read about 61 %.

checked.check: Physical charge accounting: does SOC follow measured charge?
checked.result: Yes between corrections. One 38 pp correction at 1576.5-1606.5 s has 0.0545 Ah behind it and would need about 4553 A. Delivered charge to cutoff is about 3.8 Ah against 63.6 Ah promised.
checked.about: SOC estimation error, low capacity, or current under-read

checked.check: Compare around t=640 s (cell and pack voltage shift)
checked.result: No step inside the +-100 s window (cell max 3.21 to 3.214 V, min 3.2 to 3.19 V). The shift is a gradual decline, not an abrupt event.
checked.about: Sensing fault (an abrupt channel fault is not seen)

checked.result: Cell max 3.113 to 3.081 V, min 2.991 to 2.943 V, pack 293.0 to 289.1 V. SOC only 61.2 to 60.8 %. Voltage keeps falling while SOC barely moves.
Fault level 1, 2, 3 at 1453, 1799 and 2100.5 s, then contactors open at 2100.5 s. This runs from cell under-voltage to contactor opening.
Lowest cell was index 64 in 100% of samples, but the highest cell fell 450 mV, more than the 260 mV spread. Insufficient alone.
Telemetry cannot separate SOC error, low capacity and current under-read. Documents or independent measurements are needed.
checked.about: SOC error, low capacity, current under-read

effects.why: Protective escalation following the low-cell condition.
Contactor opening is the BMS protective response (HV lost).

effects.quote: CHANGE battery.pack_current at t=2094.5 s: 6.54 -> 0 A (step -6.54, 1000x its usual variation)
effects.why: Load ended just before the trip. The recording does not show who or what commanded it. It is not the cause.

safety_findings.statement: Violation: SOC re-stated by 37.95 pp without measured charge. This is an estimator, capacity or current question, not a measured depletion.
Escalation recorded (highest level 3) but no specification to judge it. Treat as the BMS behaving as designed until thresholds are supplied.
One protective shutdown, HV not re-closed. Cells may be over-discharged, so check cell rest voltages before any further HV closure or charge.

unknowns: Whether SOC was ever calibrated at a full charge before this recording (no earlier records).
Actual usable capacity of the pack (no independent test).
Real BMS under-voltage thresholds and SOC correction logic (no specification).
